verses.1: And a voice came from heaven, saying, Abiya, Sila, and Fentos, servants of the Most High God, as you have seen these who died and rose again before you, so also you shall rise after your death, and your faces shall shine in the kingdom of heaven.
verses.2: And they went with them, those faithful men, and they became martyrs there.
verses.3: And when they had prayed and finished, they worshipped God, and death did not frighten them, nor the judgment of the king.
verses.4: And they went to them, those faithful and exalted ones, and they were not afraid of them, but were like innocent lambs; and when they came to them, they seized them and beat them and bound them and scourged them and brought them to the king and set them before him.
verses.5: And the king answered and said to them, You transgressors, why do you not offer sacrifice and bow down to my gods?
verses.6: And those holy and blessed and chosen and joyful brothers, Abiya, Sila, and Fentos, answered him, glorious ones like a precious pearl of the sea, whose root is firm, as with one mouth.
verses.7: And they said to that lawless king, As for us, we will not sacrifice nor bow down to filthy gods, which have neither heart nor understanding.
verses.8: And moreover, gold and silver, wood and stone are the work of the hands of the potter and the work of the hands of men, which have neither soul nor understanding nor mind; and they do not do good to those who do good to them, nor do they harm those who harm them.
verses.9: And the king answered them and said to them, Why do you do thus and revile my glorious gods? For they themselves know who it is that insults them and reviles them.
verses.10: And they answered and said to him, As for us, we revile them and do not honor them, for they are nothing at all in our sight.
verses.11: And the king answered and said to them, According to the evil of your deeds I will judge you, and I will make your flesh melt away with great torture and with scourging and with fire.
verses.12: And now tell me whether you will sacrifice to my gods or not; otherwise I will bring upon you the punishment of the tearing of sinews and of the sword.
verses.13: And they answered and said to him, As for us, we will not bow down nor sacrifice to filthy gods. And the king commanded that they beat them with long rods, and after that with whips, and after that they should flay them until their inward parts were exposed.
verses.14: And after this they bound them and cast them into the prison which was in the house of custody, until he should take counsel by what means to kill them and judge them.
verses.15: And they took them into the prison and bound them with heavy bonds, without mercy; and they remained in the prison three days and three nights.
verses.16: And after three days the king commanded that a herald go around, that the governors and counselors and officials and the great men of the city should be gathered together.
verses.17: And while King Tsirutsaydan was seated, he commanded that they bring those blessed ones, Abiya, Sila, and Fintos, and they brought them before him, bound and wounded.
verses.18: And the king said to them, Have you perhaps reconsidered while you remained these three days, or are you still in your former wickedness?
verses.19: And the blessed ones answered, looking up to God, and said to him, As for us, we are steadfast, and we will not consent to the defilement which you speak, which is full of evil and filth.
verses.20: And that tyrant was enraged, and commanded that they be hung up, and their wounds were reopened, and their blood flowed upon the ground.
verses.21: And again he commanded that they scrape them with iron combs and tear their flesh; and they did so. And the blessed ones said, Speak, O executioner; by your coming you have multiplied our judgment, and our reward is multiplied.
verses.22: And again he commanded that they bring savage beasts, leopards and bears and lions, that they might be set upon them, so that they would devour their flesh and thus destroy them together with their bones.
verses.23: And he commanded the keepers of the beasts that they set them upon them; and they did as he commanded them, and they bound the holy martyrs a second time, and again they bound them in the stocks which they had made for them.
verses.24: And those beasts crouched over them, purring; and when they came near to the martyrs, they bowed down to them and did obeisance to them.
verses.25: And they returned to their dens, purring; and the keepers were afraid, and they took them until they brought them before the face of the king.
verses.26: And there they killed, of the number of the nobles, five thousand souls.
verses.27: And many were broken, crying out in fear one against another, until at night the king left his throne and fled; and with difficulty they seized the beasts and took them to their dens.
verses.29: And the martyrs answered and said to their brothers, It is not fitting for us to flee after we have stood for the testimony; but if you are afraid, go and flee, you yourselves.
verses.30: And their young brothers said, We also will stand with you before the king, and if you die, we also will die with you.
verses.31: And after this the king saw, in the vision of the dream of his kingdom, that those blessed ones had been set free and were standing.
verses.32: And the king commanded that they seize the five brothers and cast them into the prison, until he should take counsel by what means to judge them; and they cast them into the prison and bound them with heavy bonds in the innermost dungeon, without mercy.
verses.33: And King Tsirutsaydan said, I know that these sorcerers and deceivers have hardened the hearts of these men; according to the hardness of their strength, so is the evil of their deeds; and when I speak, they harden and stiffen their hearts.
verses.34: And I will repay them according to the evil of their deeds, and I will burn their flesh with fire, that it may become ashes, and I will tear it there; I will scatter their flesh like chaff upon a great mountain, that the wind may carry them away.
verses.35: And after he had said this, three days passed, and he commanded that they bring the saints; and when those saints had come near, he commanded that they kindle a fire in the furnace and in a great pit, and they cast into it naphtha and pitch and firebrands, pitch and papyrus and stubble and resin of the pine and asphalt and sulfur.
verses.36: And when the furnace burned, they went to the king, his servants, saying, We have done what you commanded us; send the men who are to be thrown in.
verses.37: And he commanded that they receive them and cast them into the furnace of fire; and they did as the king commanded them, and the blessed ones entered into it, committing their souls to God.
verses.38: And the angels received them, while those who had cast them in watched them; and they took their souls into the bosom of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, into the garden of joy.
